title: Operation: Stop the Fishing Trip
text: “But… if I report to that wise and brilliant king that the ships sank and we couldn’t go, what will the people of Melromarc say about it…”
“Those bastards planned this! Doing something like this!”
“That’s right, that’s right! The wise and brilliant king must have schemed this up to make Seaetto-sama look bad!”

“No doubt about it! It’s exactly the kind of trick they’d pull! Asking us for a favor, then sinking our ships so we can’t even manage a simple fishing trip—they’re trying to laugh at us, calling us useless!”
“Some ‘reconciliation policy’ this is! Doing something like this, damn it all!”
Voices of condemnation rose up, indeed.
“Hmm… I had thought the wise king truly wished to see his daughter’s happy face, but…”
Éclair’s parent wore the face of someone who believed in Trash. And for the most part, that belief was correct.
“I have never met the man myself, so I cannot say…”

“I have heard everyone’s opinions, but at least judging from the wise king’s demeanor, I would say this was not his doing. That said, I cannot rule out the possibility that some other noble overheard and schemed this up on their own. Either way, I want the investigation into how this was done to continue.”
With words along those lines, it seemed Éclair’s and Big Sister’s parents were working to calm the villagers down.
“For now… supposing someone really is scheming to bring about our downfall by using our failure to catch fish as an excuse…”
“Even so, I think the best course is still to go and catch them, and prove them wrong…”
Éclair’s parent seemed to be asking around among the demi-human beastfolk within the territory, wondering if anyone could go.
“Even without a ship, it’s not impossible to swim there.”
“We’ve got a skilled fisherman on our side too. One we’re quite proud of.”

Big Sister’s parent puffed out their chest and smiled. Without question, they were trying to send Older Sister out without a ship! There were aquatic-type beastfolk here too, after all… My reading of the situation had been far too shallow, I say. Now that I thought of it, even in the first world, Father had let other skilled swimmers besides Older Sister settle in the village. Ngh… whatever should I do.
“Then there is nothing for it but to ask. Everyone! No matter what obstacles arise, I beg you to see this through!”

Their unity was strong indeed. Unity can certainly become strength at times, but considering the future, I could say with certainty this was not heading in a good direction. Worse still, the talk had settled into having the aquatic beastfolk carry everyone out there. They were even discussing using logs and scrap lumber as makeshift footing. Ngghhh… indeed. I could hardly go around inflicting status ailments on everyone one by one to keep them from departing. Not even I would stoop to that. Whatever should I do… was there nothing left but to resign myself to it? It seemed they intended to set out for the fishing trip the next morning as planned, once the alcohol had worn off. I did not want to give up. This was too precious a chance. I knew of the regret that awaited Older Sister. Thanks to our support, she had been putting on a cheerful face, but what followed afterward would haunt her for the rest of her life. This might be more than I alone could handle. So then, I had to think of what to do. Hmm…
Plan 1: Raid the town and village, incapacitating the fishermen. Of course, this would also mean incapacitating Éclair’s parent in the same manner.

An easy enough method, I say. I need only avoid killing anyone. If I timed it so they could move again by the time the wave struck, it might work out somehow. No matter how many came at me at once, I could handle it. The problem was… this might interfere with my other activities. Wearing a mask or cloak could mitigate things somewhat, but the trouble was that the people here were demi-humans and beastfolk with sharp noses—they would likely remember my scent. Worse, Melromarc might seize on the chaos and launch an attack before the wave even arrived, piggybacking on the confusion. It would be disastrous if I were recognized somewhere as the summoned Spear Hero. A hero acting conveniently for their purposes could easily become their rallying banner. If the Melromarc nobles and Trash became convinced of victory and jumped on the bandwagon, it would turn into far more than a mere scuffle—it would become a full-blown war. And with fewer able-bodied fighters, the margin for error would become maddeningly thin. Perhaps forcibly destroying the ships had been too hasty a move after all. …No, perhaps it would have been better to capture Éclair’s parent early on their way back to the territory and keep them confined until the wave hit. Ngh, how vexing that I had simply watched and waited. I regretted not prioritizing this over exterminating the Crimson Swine.
Plan 2: Persuade either Éclair’s parent or Big Sister’s parent.

Tell them my circumstances honestly and have them delay the fishing trip. The problem was whether they would believe me… well, I could still fall back on Plan 1 if this failed, so I’d treat it as a last resort. In the end, it would likely just lead to me getting reported and more trouble piling up. Things seemed to be lining up rather unfavorably. But compromise and giving up were not in my dictionary. Still, it was a concern that this kind of persuasion had rarely worked well for me in the past. Memories of failing to recruit Panda came flooding back. This sort of thing had always been Father’s specialty… it truly pained me that he wasn’t here. I couldn’t help but keenly feel how much better things would be if he’d been summoned alongside me before the wave. Spirit of the Spear! The least you could have done was arrange for Father to be transported along with me, I say! Honestly! Even a freshly-summoned Father, I believed, would have gone along with it—even disbelieving, out of sheer amusement—if I explained the circumstances. That the Spirit of the Spear failed to do this made it a truly troublesome spirit indeed. Bah, humbug! But grumbling wouldn’t get me anywhere, so—on to the next plan.
Plan 3: I catch the target fish myself.

Using Drive Mode and the like in combination, I could literally go fetch fish from distant waters. Furthermore, if I dressed them and brought them back via Portal, I could preserve a fair degree of freshness. The problem was just what kind of fish this target fish actually was. Apparently it was quite a rare species… that Crimson Swine, demanding such a specifically troublesome fish had to be deliberate malice. A further problem: there was a limit to how much I could carry back alone. One fish alone would be fine, but it seemed multiple were needed. Even if I did catch them, I had no connections for how to hand them over, and even funneling money through Zeltoble as an anonymous merchant donation would look suspicious. They might not even use it. And the time lost was a concern too. I’d keep this as a last resort.
Plan 4: Persuade, or else silence, Older Sister.

Let me try approaching Older Sister afterward—she had remarkably sharp instincts—and see if persuasion was possible. It seemed that in this deep-sea fishing expedition without ships, Older Sister was likely to become the linchpin of the whole operation. Indeed, among the aquatic demi-humans and beastfolk in this village and Éclair’s parent’s territory, she had a larger build and considerable skill, so naturally people would rely on her. That Older Sister would be counted on as the representative of this deep-sea fishing venture was practically inevitable. Which meant Older Sister could become my next target. Should negotiation fail, binding her so she couldn’t move would, at worst, still serve as an obstruction. At the very least, it would delay the fishing trip. So then, how should I go about it… thinking back over everything in this loop so far, perhaps simply explaining the circumstances honestly and letting her decide for herself was the way to go. Although—Older Sister had the kind of intelligence-gathering side to her that would make her capable of espionage work, so even if she nodded along, she might well leak information. I would need to earn her trust while only sharing information within safe limits. Still, as a procedure I could manage, restraining Older Sister first seemed like a sound move. If that failed, I could move on to executing the other plans I’d devised so far.
And so, I decided to try Plan 4: approaching Older Sister.

Amid the restless, anxious night following the chaos of all the ships sinking, I quietly trailed Older Sister, unnoticed, as she went to retrieve something from her secret base—an island she kept as her own private home. I had worried about having to stay close to Big Sister and her family the whole time, but thankfully the ever-cheerful Older Sister had ended up alone sooner than expected. And so, fairly soon after arriving on the island—without even stepping into the storage shed, she lit a bonfire, and turning around, Big Sister opened her mouth to speak.
“I wonder if someone’s there~?”
